solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Proud to have doctor for hospital suffering from wind

indicators.note: to have one thing for another means swapping it in, so one letter is replaced
for means instead of, so the doctor's letters replace the hospital's letter

parts.note: proud means haughty

explanation.surface: An arrogant person needs a doctor rather than hospital treatment for flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: A room full of cold air currents is literally suffering from wind blowing through it.

clue.text: Figure more or less game in retreat

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed inside the retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
CA, circa, means about or more or less
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A rough figure for a game played in retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric figure with ten sides and angles.

clue.text: Lead lost by US president, at the back

indicators.note: the president's name loses its leading letter

parts.note: William Howard Taft was a US president

explanation.surface: A US president lost the lead and ended up at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for the rear part of a ship, towards the stern.

clue.text: A cruel gent abused member of family

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cruel man mistreats a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's uncle is a relative, a member of the family.

clue.text: Person taking newspaper mainly providing coverage for another

indicators.note: the second paper wraps around the first, covering it
mainly means the paper's title loses its last letter

parts.note: another newspaper, the FT or Financial Times, with its article
i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A journalist takes one paper's story and offers it as another's coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another newspaper: THE FT, cut to THEF by 'mainly', round I. 'taking' is a link that also suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals is a kind of person.

clue.text: Stupid cheat from America

definitions.note: used as a noun, as in calling someone 'stupid', matching the noun answer

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
from gives OF and America gives US, read together as of US

explanation.surface: An American swindler is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' here is a form of address, a noun, as in 'Hey, stupid!'.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a dim, foolish person, the sort one might address as 'stupid'.

clue.text: Award comprising first for Oliver Reed

indicators.note: comprising means the award contains the letter

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: first for means take the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: An award goes to the actor Oliver Reed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the actor Oliver Reed, but 'Reed' alone is the definition. OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument, often just called a reed.

clue.text: Oil ablaze over early part of summer

indicators.note: over means on top of, the first piece placed above the second in this down entry

parts.note: ablaze means flaming
June is the first month of summer in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: Oil catches fire at the start of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' means an oil painting: Leighton's famous 1895 picture of a sleeping woman in orange.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated oil painting by Frederic Leighton, so an example of an oil.

clue.text: Upended shot is in cocktail

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, so in this down entry the pieces read bottom to top

parts.note: shot means raced, sped off
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shot glass is upended into a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upended' turns RACED IS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: List of woes in French I note in register

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: the second in means the note goes inside the register's word

parts.note: a meter registers or reads a value
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A list of complaints written in French, with a note in the register.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lament or tale of woe, named after the prophet Jeremiah.

clue.text: Queen say divorced by the king; he and I now entangled a queen

definitions.note: she is one example of a queen, hence 'say'

indicators.note: the card is split apart, its two halves divorced from each other by the material put between them

parts.note: a queen is a playing card
THE plus R, the abbreviation for king (Rex)

indicators.note: the words he and I now are tangled up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A queen divorced by her king laments a tangled marriage involving three people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entangled' rearranges HE I NOW; 'divorced by' splits the card in two around the inserted letters. She was beheaded, not divorced, by Henry VIII, so the surface is historically off.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's fifth wife was a queen of England, so she is an example of a queen.

clue.text: As would a pillow in your dreams!

definitions.meaning: a pillow is filled with padding, which is what this phrase literally describes happening to it
a rude refusal or dismissal, telling someone their hope will never come true

explanation.walkthrough: The blog thought this clunky: the first sense needs 'would' to be read as 'would do'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal description of filling a cushion and a crude British brush-off.

clue.text: Happy as Larry used hands to catch salmon?

parts.note: tickling is catching fish, especially trout, by stroking them by hand
salmon is a shade of pink

explanation.surface: A happy fisherman caught a salmon with his bare hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy as Larry' is a British idiom for extremely happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean delighted or very pleased.

clue.text: Metal zip almost caught

indicators.note: almost means the word for zip loses its final letter

parts.note: zip means energy or zing
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A metal zip almost got stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluish-white metallic element used in galvanising steel.

clue.text: See adult very disheartened about time out of school

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters are turned about into a new order
disheartened means the word very loses its heart, its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A dejected adult sees about some time off school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes ER from VERY, leaving VY; 'about' rearranges SEEADULT plus VY.
explanation.definitionFit: A period when pupils are excused lessons to revise at home for exams.

clue.text: Party without tins? Find another mug!

parts.note: having no tins means no can, the word used loosely for the whole lot
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party with no tinned drinks prompts someone to say they won't be fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog called this clunky: the refusal 'find another mug!' means 'I'm not your sucker, ask someone else'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal refusals: the speaker won't do it and tells the asker to find someone else to exploit.

clue.text: Sleepy old Scandinavian, sorry to be tucked in

indicators.note: the apology is tucked inside the Scandinavian word

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian
'sorry?' and 'eh?' both ask someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A sleepy old Scandinavian apologises before being tucked into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dull place is called a one-horse town, so it means sleepy or backward.

clue.text: Number Ten I suspect joins many leaving country

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the words ten and I are not to be trusted as written
leaving means the word many goes out of the country's name

parts.note: Germany is a European country

explanation.surface: Ten, I think, joins a crowd emigrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges TEN I into INTE; GERMANY with MANY leaving gives GER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number, with no fractional part, is a kind of number.

clue.text: Joy has nearly landed in Middle Eastern region

indicators.note: has means holds, so the word for joy contains the other piece

parts.note: joy means glee

indicators.note: nearly means the word for landed is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to alight is to land, so landed is alit

explanation.surface: A joyful person has nearly arrived in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy has' reads as a person named Joy, but it is the word for joy holding the shortened landed.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern part of historical Palestine, now in Israel, is a region of the Middle East.

clue.text: Party drink for animated figure?

parts.note: a gala is a festive party
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A party drink for a cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' suggests cartoons; it means brought to life.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, Pygmalion's statue was brought to life, so she is a figure animated.

clue.text: Executed, French novelist drops a poor baby!

parts.note: executed means carried out, did

indicators.note: drops means the novelist's name loses the letter given

parts.note: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A French writer is put to death, and someone mocks with 'poor baby!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-sympathetic exclamation used to someone making a fuss, like 'poor little thing!'.

clue.text: That's the same for every fish

parts.note: snap is the call when two matching cards appear, so it means the same
per means for every, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: The same goes for every fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of edible tropical sea fish.

clue.text: Somewhere to swim with cap and ring

parts.note: a cap or top is a lid
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A swimming spot where you wear a cap and use a ring float.
explanation.definitionFit: A public open-air swimming pool, a common British term for one.

clue.text: TIME follows HERB at end of my word chain

indicators.note: at end of means the herb comes after the exclamation
follows means the time comes after the herb

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my word!'
dill is a herb
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Instructions for a word chain game: time follows herb at the end of my word.
explanation.definitionFit: A long chain of mountains, as in the Andes, is called this.

clue.text: Introduction to dictionary split meaning

indicators.note: introduction to means the opening letter of dictionary

parts.note: a rift is a split

explanation.surface: An introduction to a dictionary splits word meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general meaning or gist.

clue.text: Hold up free clothing round designer

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the reversed word encloses the letter
hold up in a down clue means lift, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to rid is to free
O is round

explanation.surface: Free clothing is held up near a designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was a famous French fashion designer.

clue.text: Picture Philip getting upset with assistant

indicators.note: upset means overturned or mixed up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Philip becomes cross with his helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' is the film sense: a 1984 mock-documentary about a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion picture, the famous spoof rock documentary film.

clue.text: Raised flat cap

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: mat or matt means flat, without shine

explanation.surface: A flat cap is lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tam-o'-shanter, a Scottish woollen cap.

clue.text: An alcoholic drink knocked back in capital

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: knocked back means the drink is read the other way round, and also suits drinking in the surface

parts.note: arak is an anise-flavoured spirit of the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone downs a strong drink in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: Ship carrying Republican flag

indicators.note: carrying means the ship holds the letter within it

parts.note: a steamer is a ship

explanation.surface: A ship flies a Republican flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag or pennant flown from a mast.
